prompt_en: Create a photorealistic editorial environmental portrait in a salt-weathered coastal observatory during an approaching storm. An unmistakably adult original fictional weather observer, with a facial structure designed independently from the reference portrait, has long dark wavy hair and wears a dark flowing blouse inspired only by the visible styling of the reference. At a brass workbench, she carefully rotates a sealed cylindrical storm-glass instrument while recording the changing sea pressure. The frame clearly shows her active hand, the full instrument, a rain-lashed window, lighthouse beams, and sea spray. Make the central optical event face pareidolia embedded in a nonface material. Within the transparent cylinder, ordinary fernlike crystals, two small air bubbles, and one curved band of dark sediment accidentally align into a vivid face-like configuration. In this weather-appliance context, a clearly nonface wood rock cloud facade or appliance provides the source, and the sealed storm glass is unmistakably that ordinary source object. Two eye-like marks and one mouth-like interval create the face relation: the air bubbles become eye-like spots while the sediment curve supplies the mouth-like interval. Across the illusion, original grain texture structure or atmosphere continues through every apparent feature, expressed here by uninterrupted liquid, crystal, bubble, and sediment structure. At a single viewing distance, the face-like arrangement and original nonface source remain simultaneously readable, with the full instrument legible around the pattern. Ordinary substrate parts create the reading through their viewpoint and spacing; instrument crystals, bubbles, and sediment remain materially ordinary at native detail. Use a three-quarter medium-wide composition with the storm glass large enough for thumbnail recognition. Cool storm daylight and one warm task lamp share plausible reflections across skin, black fabric, brass, and curved glass. Keep crisp optical detail and enough depth of field for the hand, instrument, and material face relation to read together.
